title: Adversaries with Limited Information in the Friedkin-Johnsen Model

problem.claim: The work concerns adversaries who alter the opinions of a small set of users to increase disagreement and polarization in online social networks.

gap.claim: Prior work commonly assumes that the adversary knows the network topology and all user opinions, although user opinions may be unavailable or difficult to estimate accurately.

contributions.claim: Uses the Friedkin–Johnsen opinion-formation model to mathematically study the amount of discord an adversary can produce.

narrative_sequence.summary: Online social networks have been targeted by adversaries seeking to introduce discord and destabilize communities.
The adversarial goal may be to increase disagreement and polarization rather than support one side.
Opinion-formation models such as the Friedkin–Johnsen model provide a mathematical framework for studying these attacks.
Existing work commonly assumes full knowledge of network topology and user opinions.
Full knowledge of user opinions can be unrealistic because opinions may be unavailable or difficult to estimate accurately.

source_observation.claim: Full knowledge of user opinions may be unavailable or inaccurate.

interpretation.claim: Adversarial or robustness analyses should account for information limitations rather than assuming perfect observability.

application.claim: Model attack effectiveness under partial or uncertain knowledge of user opinions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how limited information changes attack effectiveness.

unknowns: The specific limited-information adversary model is not described.
No theoretical results, empirical findings, datasets, metrics, or comparisons are reported.
